title: Radiomics Signatures and Patient Outcomes in Intracerebral Hemorrhage
text:
Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is a severely debilitating cerebrovascular disease, which affects over 70,000
patients per year in the U.S., and is responsible for over half of stroke-related disability worldwide. So far, the
diagnosis, surveillance, and prediction of outcome in intracerebral hemorrhage have mainly relied on visual and
subjective assessment of head CT scans. Computerized assessment of medical images and machine learning
algorithms can extract hidden features from CT scans and provide innovative tools for accurate outcome
prediction and personalized treatment decisions in patients with hemorrhagic stroke.

title: The role of cholesterol biosynthesis in metastatic and recurrent endometrialcancer
text:
Although early-stage and low grade endometrial cancer generally exhibits a favorable prognosis, metastatic
and recurrent endometrial cancer is incurable with currently available standard therapies for most women.
Therefore, there is an urgent obligation to explore the mechanism of tumor metastasis and recurrence to
further elucidate the progression of endometrial cancer. The experiments proposed in this application will
employ the first preclinical animal model that closely resembles human endometrial cancer with distant
metastasis and recurrence to identify new mechanistic targets that could dramatically improve therapeutic
options for endometrial cancer.

title: Avian-inspired Regenerative Therapies for Hearing Loss
text:
This research project aims to unravel the mechanisms underlying the quiescent and non-regenerative nature of
cochlear supporting cells in adult mice, shedding light on their molecular and epigenetic signatures. Through a
comprehensive characterization of these cells under both normal and damage-induced conditions, this study will
provide critical insights into the barriers that impede their ability to re-enter the cell cycle and regenerate hair
cells. By leveraging these insights, the project aims to develop innovative therapeutic strategies that can
effectively restore hearing in humans, aligning with the NIH's mission to alleviate the burden of human illness
and disability.

title: Identifying causal gene programs for vascular disease using high throughput CRISPR genomics
text:
Overall Component
Genes and pathways that underlie genetic risk for vascular diseases of the heart and lung remain poorly
characterized and challenging to identify and treat. To address these challenges, our multidisciplinary team has
developed novel genomics tools to vastly accelerate studies of genes and pathways underlying heart and lung
diseases. These innovative tools will enable our overall goal to systematically study large numbers of candidate
disease genes; define how they integrate into gene programs in vascular cells; test how these programs differ
across cell types, vascular beds, disease conditions, and biological sex; and thus, identify new genes and
pathways that influence risk for vascular diseases.

title: Mechanism of HIV-1 Env Neutralization by Antibodies Targeting the Membrane-Proximal External Region
text:
This application will provide unprecedented insights into the structure, function and dynamics of anti-MPER
bnAbs engagement with the epitopes on HIV-1 Env trimer in a native environment and reveal the mechanism
on HIV-1 membrane fusion inhibition. The long-term goal is to correlate these structures with their functions to
design improved immunogens and guide the development of an effective HIV-1 vaccine.

title: Training Grant in Precision Cancer Control
text:
The ability to precisely target individuals with cancer and at-risk populations with evidence-based tools to address
individual, sociocultural, or environmental factors is likely to lead to the greatest improvements in cancer
outcomes and reductions in cancer risk. Thus, this application for a new T32 postdoctoral training program at
Fox Chase Cancer Center is designed to prepare PhD and MD postdoctoral fellows to lead innovative and
scientifically rigorous research in precision cancer control with diverse populations.

title: Development of a multifunctional, acoustofluidic 3D bioprinter with single-cell resolution
text:
Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting has shown tremendous potential in constructing customized tissue models
and implantable tissues. However, existing 3D bioprinters are incapable of printing biomimetic tissues with the
resolution, complexity, and functions as native tissues. The proposed research will develop an acoustics-based
3D bioprinting technology, which overcomes these obstacles and enables biocompatible, fast, and scalable
printing of functional biomimetic tissues with high resolution and complex features such as controlled anisotropic
properties, high cell densities, and biomimetic cellular architectures.

title: Biomarker Signatures of TB Infection in Young Children With and Without HIV
text:
Current approaches to diagnosis and management of children < 5 years that are at high risk of TB and have
a high case-fatality rate are inadequate. We anticipate promising integrated biomarkers that will transform
public health and clinical interventions in this most vulnerable population by providing novel approaches to
risk-stratify children <5 years of age at risk for TB for targeting the administration of preventive therapy and
ATT.

title: An-in-depth exploration of coping strategies and their impact on psychological distress in cancer survivors
text: This research proposal addresses NIH’s commitment to prevent and mitigate cancer disparities and aligns with NCI’s key research area of cancer survivorship, which among other issues prioritizes addressing psychological concerns in cancer survivors. Overall, findings from this predoctoral (F99) to postdoctoral (K00) research project will be an important first step in guiding the development of psychological distress management interventions and programs for cancer survivors, with the aim of ensuring improved quality of life and survival

title: Rapid Automatic Diagnosis of Palpable Breast Lumps Without a Radiologist or Sonographer
text: This project will develop and validate a scalable ultrasound imaging system that combines volume sweep imaging and artificial intelligence to improve rapid assessment of palpable breast abnormalities. Peru provides a unique setting for evaluation of this system because women frequently present with symptomatic breast abnormalities and often experience delayed access to imaging, creating a research opportunity not readily available in the United States. Findings from this work will support implementation of accessible breast imaging pathways to improve timely breast cancer diagnosis for medically underserved populations in the United States.

title: Polarity dysregulation in Alzheimer’s disease
text:
This is an administrative supplement application to the parent grant to support the purchase of a new
microscope system due to the unexpected failure of a critical component in our existing system. There is a
critical need for a sustainable solution as our proposed aims rely heavily on high resolution confocal
microscopy. The proposed solution represents the most cost-effective way to restoring full research
productivity.

title: Determinants of pegivirus persistence and immune control
text:
Approximately 15% of the global human population is chronically infected with human pegivirus (HPgV), yet we
know very little about how this virus evades the immune system or the long term impact of chronic HPgV infection
on the human host. We have developed a mouse-adapted pegivirus (maPgV) that recapitulates several aspects
of HPgV infection including: persistent high-titer viremia; lack of overt disease; and immune-mediated clearance
of maPgV infection in a subset (~10%) of individuals. In this project, we will use our maPgV model to study
aspects of PgV persistence and immunity, with the ultimate goal of uncovering the novel mechanism by which
maPgV evades the immune system and maintains high levels in the blood of infected individuals.

title: Secondary Molecular Imaging (SMI) for head and neck cancer
text:
The current standard of care for evaluation and surveillance of regional and metastatic disease in
head and neck squamous cell carcinoma is 18F-FDG PET/CT scan, which is highly sensitive but
not specific. Due to its nonspecific targeting of any tissue with high metabolism, FDG PET/CT
produces a significant number of indeterminate findings and is of limited use for detecting tumors
located in areas of high metabolic activity. To address this, we propose that imaging using a
tumor-specific PET radiopharmaceutical can improve diagnostic specificity in head and neck
cancer patients.

title: Simulation, modelling, and estimation of direct and indirect genetic architectures and intergenerational dynamics
text:
Large-scale genetic studies of humans have identified thousands of associations between genetic variants and
human traits and diseases. However, associations can arise due to confounding factors: principally gene-
environment correlations due to indirect genetic effects (effects of relatives’ genotypes mediated through the
environment) and population stratification, and correlations with other genetic variants due to assortative mating
and population structure. Here we develop an advanced simulation software package to study the breadth of
this problem as well as novel theory and methods that enable robust estimation of indirect genetic effects and
the impact of assortative mating.

title: Instrumentation and Services Core
text:
The Mississippi INBRE Instrumentation and Services Core provides essential research 
infrastructure in the form of advanced instrumentation and also expertise. The capabilities offered through this 
Core are essential for the completeness of biomedical research in Mississippi. This will be accomplished by 1) 
providing access to instruments and expertise, 2) educate researchers and students in cutting-edge 
approaches, and 3) maintaining the competitive edge of Core services.

title: Enhancing the Effectiveness of Immunotherapies by T Cell Epigenetic Reprogramming
text:
Despite the unprecedent success of T cell immunotherapies in treating some previously refractory cancers,
terminal exhaustion of chronically stimulated T cells remains a major obstacle to achieving durable protective
immune responses. We discovered a novel approach to synergize the efficacy of T cell immunotherapies by
modulating microenvironmental signals that regulate T cell-intrinsic epigenetic programs. The goals of this grant
are to identify the role of these upstream regulators of the epigenetic programs specific to terminally-exhausted
T cells, and to re-route their epigenetic programming toward the functional state.

title: AIDS Clinical Trial Group Laboratory Center
text:
The laboratory studies proposed in this application will have a direct beneficial effect on the health of millions of
patients worldwide who are infected with HIV, TB and Hepatitis B, transforming the treatment of patients with
these infections. The clinical research conducted by the ACTG will lead to significantly reduced morbidity and
mortality, particularly among populations disproportionately affected by HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis.

title: Comprehensive Research Experiences to Advance Training and Education (CREATE) for Future Cancer Researchers
text:
In the United States in 2025, there will be more than 2 million new cancer cases (excluding non-melanoma skin
cancers) and more than 618,000 people will die from cancer. It is imperative to start training the next
generation of cancer researchers as early as possible in order to sustain conceptual as well as therapeutic
innovation to reduce disease burden. This is a renewal application for a comprehensive summer
undergraduate research program that integrates mentored cancer research with educational initiatives in drug
discovery, computational and public health-based approaches to provide research experiences and skills that
will facilitate successful entry into oncology research careers.

title: Shared Resource 09: Hematological Tissue Bank Shared Resource (HTBSR)
text: PROJECT SUMMARY – HEMATOLOGY TISSUE BANK SHARED RESOURCE (HTBSR) The Ohio State University Comprehensive Cancer Center (OSUCCC) Hematology Tissue Bank Shared Resource (HTBSR) is a longstanding biobank, established in 1997, that procures, processes, and stores biologic material from consenting patients with hematologic diseases. The HTBSR procures samples in two ways: 1) via a general biobanking protocol for future research; and 2) via specific clinical research protocols with special collection needs. The major services of the HTBSR are consenting patients, procuring samples (e.g., blood, bone marrow, and leukapheresis products) as directed by the general or a specific IRB protocol, assessing sample quality, providing fresh samples to investigators or processing them for storage, providing an oversight process for use of samples and data, and delivering de-identified samples and data to approved recipients. Investigators receive samples identified phenotypically or genetically, along with clinical data and available pathology data (including standard of care immunophenotyping and genetic sequencing panels). During the current cycle, Dr. Lapo AlinariLHM served as the HTBSR Director. The Specific Aims of the HTBSR are to: 1) consent subjects and procure samples from patients with hematologic diseases; 2) uniformly process, characterize and store biospecimens using state-of-the art procedures; and 3) provide de-identified biospecimens with associated clinical, pathological and genomic data to OSUCCC researchers and to outside institutions so that they can correlate findings from patient samples with clinical or population-based outcomes. In addition to biospecimens procured from consented patients with hematologic diseases, the HTBSR procures, processes, and distributes fresh or cryopreserved peripheral blood samples from healthy donors, peripheral blood and bone marrow samples from allogeneic stem cell transplant recipients, and cell-therapy patients (Cell Therapy Bank), collects and distributes discarded normal hipbone from replacement surgeries as a source of marrow stromal cells and umbilical cord blood as a source of CD34+ hematopoietic stem cells. In the next funding cycle, the HTBSR will continue to expand its breadth of tissue procurement services, addressing the OSUCCC research priorities of immuno-oncology, cancer engineering, and cancer prevention and survivorship, will continue to improve the electronic workflows regarding patient identification and sample annotation, and will expand its operations to the new West Campus outpatient care facility.

title: University of Michigan Training Program in Genomic Science
text: This proposal seeks continued support for the University of Michigan Genome Science Training Program (GSTP). The goal of the GSTP is to train graduate students to be leaders working at the interface of genetics and genomics and the mathematical and computational sciences, a critical area of genome science in which well-trained individuals are in high demand and short supply. The GSTP has a demonstrated record of success having trained >150 scientists and leaders in genome science.
